security_audit.summary: Most static findings are false positives from Markdown fences, inline code, or static Python SDK imports. One high-confidence issue remains: the Direct Line key listing example prints channel secrets, which can expose credentials.

remediation.issue: The Direct Line key example prints secret channel keys.
remediation.suggestion: Mask keys in examples and direct users to store retrieved secrets in Key Vault or another managed secret store.

content.user_title: Manage Azure Bot Service with Python
content.value_statement: Azure bot teams need reliable examples for managing bots, channels, and OAuth connections. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code through Azure Bot Service SDK workflows.
actual_capabilities: Shows AzureBotService authentication with DefaultAzureCredential and subscription configuration.
Demonstrates creating, reading, updating, listing, and deleting bot resources.
Provides examples for Microsoft Teams, Direct Line, and Web Chat channels.
Shows how to list channel details, Direct Line keys, and bot connections.
Explains SKU options, channel types, and client operation groups.
Includes OAuth connection setup using an environment-based client secret.
limitations: Does not validate Azure permissions, subscription quotas, or tenant policies.
Does not deploy bot application code or messaging endpoints.
Requires installed Azure SDK packages and authenticated Azure credentials.
Some examples can expose secrets if copied without redaction.

use_cases.title: Provision development bots
use_cases.description: Create low-cost Azure Bot Service resources and basic channels for test environments.

use_cases.title: Audit bot channel configuration
use_cases.description: List bots, channels, SKUs, and connection settings before planned changes.

use_cases.title: Integrate OAuth-backed bots
use_cases.description: Set up connection settings that use service providers and scoped permissions.

prompt_templates.title: List my bot resources
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to show how to authenticate and list Azure Bot Service bots in my subscription.

prompt_templates.title: Create a test bot
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to draft Python steps for creating an F0 Azure Bot Service with a placeholder endpoint.

prompt_templates.title: Configure channels safely
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to add Teams, Direct Line, and Web Chat channels. Include secret-handling cautions.

prompt_templates.title: Plan an OAuth connection rollout
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to outline Python SDK steps for creating a bot OAuth connection with environment-managed secrets and validation checks.

output_examples.input: List Bot Service resources in a resource group.
output_examples.output: The response would describe credential setup, resource group selection, bot listing, and fields to review, such as name, endpoint, and SKU.

output_examples.input: Create a Direct Line channel for an existing bot.
output_examples.output: The response would outline channel creation, site configuration, key handling, and follow-up validation in Azure.

output_examples.input: Prepare OAuth connection settings for Microsoft Graph.
output_examples.output: The response would identify required IDs, scopes, secret source, Azure API call sequence, and post-deployment checks.

best_practices: Use DefaultAzureCredential with least privilege roles for each Azure environment.
Store OAuth client secrets and Direct Line keys in a managed secret store.
Mask or omit generated keys before sharing logs, transcripts, or review output.
anti_patterns: Printing channel keys or OAuth secrets in chat, logs, or CI output.
Running delete examples without confirming the subscription, resource group, and bot name.
Using production endpoints or credentials in copied sample code.

faq.question: What Azure service does this skill cover?
faq.answer: It covers Azure Bot Service management through the Python Azure management SDK.

faq.question: Can it create and delete bots?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes SDK examples for creating, updating, listing, retrieving, and deleting bot resources.

faq.question: Does it manage bot application code?
faq.answer: No. It manages Azure Bot Service resources, not the bot runtime application.

faq.question: Which channels are shown?
faq.answer: The examples show Teams, Direct Line, Web Chat, and reference other common channel classes.

faq.question: How should secrets be handled?
faq.answer: Use environment variables, Key Vault, or another managed secret store. Never print real keys.

faq.question: Which AI tools can use it?
faq.answer: It is prepared for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code workflows.
